skill.name: tunit
skill.description: Run the repository TUnit Playwright test suite with dotnet commands, optional filters, limited parallelism, and report output guidance.
skill.summary: Guides agents through running TUnit Playwright tests for the SummitUI project.
skill.author: AndreHogberg

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code spans, and normal TUnit Playwright terminology. The skill documents fixed local dotnet test commands and shows no prompt injection, obfuscation, exfiltration, or reconnaissance intent.

remediation.issue: Local test commands execute repository code when an agent runs them.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should run the commands only in trusted workspaces and review test setup before execution.

content.value_statement: Running the correct TUnit Playwright command can be slow to remember. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused commands for local test execution.
actual_capabilities: Provides the command to run the full TUnit Playwright test project.
Shows how to limit parallel test execution to one or two tests.
Explains TUnit treenode filters for class, test name, and namespace selection.
Gives examples for Select accessibility tests and keyboard-pattern test filters.
Documents console-detailed and TRX report options for test output.
Summarizes project files that control retries, setup, teardown, and timeouts.
limitations: It is tailored to the SummitUI TUnit Playwright project layout.
It does not install .NET, Playwright browsers, or project dependencies.
It can only report failures that appear in available test output.
Running commands may execute local repository code and start a local server.

use_cases.title: Run the full browser test suite
use_cases.description: Use the default project command to run all TUnit Playwright tests and summarize pass or fail status.

use_cases.title: Investigate a failing component test
use_cases.description: Use treenode filters to run one class or one named test while debugging a focused failure.

use_cases.title: Collect repeatable test reports
use_cases.description: Run tests with detailed console output or TRX reports for review in development workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run all tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete test run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the TUnit Playwright test suite and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run tests sequentially
prompt_templates.scenario: Reduce load while checking browser tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the TUnit Playwright tests with maximum parallelism set to one and report any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Run one test class
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on a component or accessibility test class.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run only the Select accessibility TUnit Playwright tests and summarize failed assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a focused report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging with filtering and report output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the matching keyboard-focused Playwright tests with detailed output and tell me which failures need code changes.

output_examples.output: The agent runs the local test project, then reports the overall status, failed test names, and important error messages.
The agent uses a class-level TUnit filter, then summarizes results for that focused accessibility test group.

output_examples.input: Generate a test report for failures.
output_examples.output: The agent chooses a supported report option and explains where the report output can be reviewed.

best_practices: Start with sequential execution when Playwright tests are resource intensive.
Use the narrowest treenode filter that still covers the suspected failure.
Review failed test output before rerunning to avoid hiding real regressions.
anti_patterns: Do not run the full suite repeatedly when one focused filter is enough.
Do not ignore setup failures from the Blazor server readiness check.
Do not assume a retry means the underlying failure is harmless.

faq.question: What test framework does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports the TUnit Playwright test project described in the skill file.

faq.question: Can it run a single test class?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides treenode filter patterns for class-level and test-name selection.

faq.question: Can it reduce Playwright resource usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows commands that limit maximum parallel test execution.

faq.question: Does it install missing dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The workspace must already have the required .NET and Playwright setup.

faq.question: Does it support test reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents detailed console output and TRX report options.

faq.question: Is it safe to use in any repository?
faq.answer: Use it in trusted workspaces because running tests executes local project code.
